draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Munroe Island! It's actually eight small islets where Ashtamudi Lake meets the Kallada River, about 13.4 square km in all. People call it the Sinking Island of Kerala.
draft.hungryLine: My notes don't name anywhere to eat on the island itself, but Kollam, about 25 km away by road, is famous for its mutton and fish places.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Pulimoottil Devi Temple is a 10 min walk, and the red brick Dutch Church sits on the banks of Ashtamudi Lake. Then get in a canoe and go where the houseboats can't.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a spot by the Dutch Church on the lake bank and just watch the water.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The island is named after Colonel John Munro, a Resident of the old princely state of Travancore.

legends.title: The Sinking Island
legends.body: Around Kerala, Munroe Island has a nickname, the Sinking Island of Kerala. Ask the people who live here what it means to them.

legends.title: One family, a whole village
legends.body: Only one Christian family lives near the Dutch Church and looks after it. Its yearly festival happens with the help of the Hindu neighbours, a lovely bit of island harmony.

tips.title: Take a canoe tour.
tips.body: Vijeesh runs canoe tours through the village for about ₹300 per person, and a rickshaw from Kollam is about ₹400.

tips.title: Climb the lighthouse in the afternoon.
tips.body: If you head into Kollam, Thangassery Lighthouse is open to climb from 3-5PM.

story.title: Portuguese Kollam
story.body: Down the road in Kollam, the Portuguese set up the Infant Jesus Cathedral in 1614. Thangassery still has remnants of Portuguese and Dutch forts.

story.title: A Resident's name
story.body: The islands were named in honour of Colonel John Munro, Resident of the princely state of Travancore. Locally the village is Mundrothuruth.

story.title: The Dutch Church
story.body: The Dutch built a red brick church on the banks of Ashtamudi Lake in 1878. It mixes Dutch and Kerala styles.

story.title: A small community
story.body: The 2011 census counted 9054 people in Mundrothuruth village. The island is reachable by road, rail and water.

story.title: By canoe
story.body: Canoe tours now take visitors right through the village to see island life up close. Tell me what you spotted from the water.
